subproblem.title: Upper bound on compact sets from sub-subsequence comparisons on thickenings (parent step 2(b); Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(13))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; and (b′) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are a set W ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ with limsup_{i→∞} μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). Then limsup_{j→∞} μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ limsup (fun i => μs (ψ (φ' i)) W) atTop ≤ μ W) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(b) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4: (12), chapter-07.txt line 260; the bound before (13), lines 265–275; (13), line 276; and the subsequence-of-subsequence remark, lines 278–280). The current-specific input (the local comparison with the competitor S := C, converted to measures) is abstracted into hypothesis (b′); the remaining measure-theoretic argument is copied from the parent. No sibling result is used.
1. Fix a compact K and put L := limsup_j μ_j(K) ∈ [0, ∞].
2. (Claim: L ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for every ε > 0.) Fix ε > 0 and suppose instead that a := μ(thickening(ε, K)) < L. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, choose b with a < b < L. Since b < limsup_j μ_j(K), μ_j(K) > b for infinitely many j (frequently in atTop; Mathlib frequently_lt_of_lt_limsup). Hence there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i (Mathlib Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
3. Apply (b′) to K, ε and ψ: there are W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). By monotonicity of measures, μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(K) > b for every i, so limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ b (Mathlib le_limsup_of_frequently_le). Also μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) = a. Hence b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ a < b, a contradiction. This proves the claim.
4. (Continuity from above.) K is compact, hence closed. thickening(1, K) ⊆ cthickening(1, K), and cthickening(1, K) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P; Mathlib IsCompact.cthickening), so μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a). The open sets thickening(r, K) decrease as r ↓ 0 and their intersection is closure K = K. By continuity of measure from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed, which needs exactly one finite μ(thickening(R, K)) with R > 0 and K closed), μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r → 0⁺.
5. By step 2, L ≤ μ(thickening(r, K)) for every r > 0. Since the right side tends to μ(K) as r → 0⁺ and the order interval [L, ∞] is closed, L ≤ μ(K). As K was arbitrary, the claim holds for every compact K. ∎
proof_key_steps: If μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b < limsup_j μ_j(K), extract a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i.
Hypothesis (b′) along ψ gives W ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W); monotonicity gives b ≤ limsup ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, a contradiction.
μ(thickening(1, K)) < ∞ by finiteness on the compact cthickening(1, K); continuity from above gives μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r ↓ 0, hence limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).

audit.reason: The bad-subsequence extraction and sub-subsequence comparison establish every thickening bound. Compactness supplies a finite thickening, permitting continuity from above. Only measure monotonicity is used on W, so no measurability assumption is missing.
